Explanation: The Luxury Listing is the Core Value Unit: a Seller-created offer for a pre-owned designer item, including images, description, condition and price. Tradesy did not take inventory; the listing made Seller-held goods searchable and purchasable.
Tradesy operated the U.S. peer-to-peer luxury resale marketplace immediately before Vestiaire Collective announced its acquisition on March 15, 2022.
Tradesy needed to make peer-to-peer luxury transactions easy and trustworthy enough to compete with inventory-heavy consignment models.
More high-quality listings and Buyer demand increased transaction liquidity and commission revenue without requiring Tradesy to buy inventory.
Counterfeits, fraud, returns and inconsistent Seller execution threatened trust, while marketplace liquidity had to compete with larger resale networks.
Tradesy coordinated listing discovery, payment, Seller proceeds, returns and trust mechanisms around the direct Seller-to-Buyer exchange.
Transaction Flows: ← Consumer · Order / Pay — Buyers placed orders and paid through Tradesy's marketplace transaction flow. | → Consumer · Discovery / Protect — Tradesy provided luxury discovery, payment coordination, returns and authenticity-related marketplace protection. | ← Provider · Listing / Commission — Sellers supplied listings and paid Tradesy a commission when an item sold. | → Provider · Demand / Payout — Tradesy exposed listings to Buyer demand and coordinated Seller proceeds after a completed transaction. | → Partner · Workloads / Fees — Tradesy moved marketplace infrastructure workloads and associated cloud spending into the Google Cloud and Insight relationship. | ← Partner · Cloud / Support — Google Cloud and Insight returned scalable infrastructure, migration execution and technical support to Tradesy.

Explanation: Tradesy governed listing quality, fraud, authenticity disputes, Seller performance and its return and authenticity guarantee.
Tradesy attracted users through search, fashion media, social channels, referrals and its luxury-resale positioning.
Tradesy operated discovery, pricing technology, photo enhancement, payments, returns, customer support, fraud detection and marketplace trust.
Its member network, luxury transaction data, pricing and fraud technology, marketplace software and trust processes were key resources.
Fashion-conscious Buyers searched Tradesy for pre-owned designer handbags, clothing, shoes and accessories at prices below primary-market retail.
Buyers wanted desirable luxury and designer pieces at lower prices without accepting the full counterfeit and transaction risk of an unstructured resale market.
Tradesy offered curated luxury discovery, a clean shopping interface, returns support and an authenticity guarantee.
Luxury resale creates uncertainty around authenticity, condition, fit, pricing and shipping time.
Buyers purchased through Tradesy's marketplace transaction and payment flow rather than paying Sellers off-platform.

Individuals, collectors and professional luxury resellers supplied the inventory while keeping physical possession until a sale.

Tradesy provided luxury-focused demand, pricing recommendations, photo enhancement, shipping support and marketplace trust.
Sellers faced commission costs, uncertain time-to-sale, payout timing and the work of preparing and shipping the item.

Sellers listed through Tradesy's app and web tools and could use platform pricing and image-assistance features.
Sellers photographed, described and priced items, communicated as needed and fulfilled sold orders.

Tradesy used Google Cloud as core computing infrastructure and Insight as the specialist migration Partner that helped move its CDN, databases, data warehouse and production workloads away from earlier cloud infrastructure.
The cloud Partners had to provide reliable, elastic infrastructure and migration expertise for a rapidly growing image-, data- and transaction-heavy marketplace.
Tradesy's production workloads created cloud consumption and a strategic customer relationship for Google Cloud and Insight.
Moving databases, CDN, analytics and production workloads created technical migration risk and required continuity for marketplace users.
Tradesy moved workloads and cloud spending to the Partner stack; Google Cloud and Insight returned infrastructure, migration support and operational expertise.
